analysis.one_liner: Tata Power is an integrated power company that generates (coal, hydro, renewables), transmits and distributes electricity, and is now expanding into EV charging and grid infrastructure for data centres.
analysis.whats_happening: Tata Power Renewable Energy commissioned 419 MW of utility-scale capacity in Q2 FY27 (up 130% YoY), taking its operating renewables portfolio to 7.2 GW, and the company separately committed ₹15,000 crore to upgrade the Mumbai grid for AI data centres (announced 14 Oct 2026). Its Mundra plant, shut for nine months in FY26 pending a new power-purchase agreement, is back running but only under a government Section 11 directive now extended to 31 December 2026 while the underlying agreement with states is still being finalised. The board meets on 11 November 2026 to approve Q2 FY27 results (quarter and half-year ended 30 September 2026).
analysis.plain_terms: The core business — selling and moving electricity, plus the fast-growing renewables arm — is genuinely expanding: revenue, EBITDA and profit from these segments were all up double digits in the June 2026 quarter. But the company is funding this growth with a lot of borrowed money, and its Mundra coal plant has a history of being ordered to run or shut by the government rather than operating on a normal commercial contract, which cost it ₹800 crore in lost capacity charges last year. The stock trades at a premium valuation versus a typical power utility, which only makes sense if the renewables and data-centre bets pay off as planned.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (Jun-26): consolidated PAT (owners' share) ₹1,176 crore, up 11% YoY; revenue ₹19,051 crore, up 5.6%; EBITDA ₹4,249 crore, up 8.1%. Management flagged that the core generation/T&D/renewables businesses grew revenue, EBITDA and PAT by 12%, 12% and 14% respectively — broad-based, not a one-line distortion. Solar cell & module manufacturing PAT of ₹371 crore was described as 'nearly 4x' higher YoY — that comparison is off a small base from a scaling-up business and should not be read as a 4x improvement in the underlying franchise. Q4 FY26 (Mar-26): PAT ₹1,415.5 crore (+8.4% YoY, +18.5% QoQ) even as revenue fell 12.85% YoY to ₹14,900 crore — a revenue/profit divergence whose cause (likely a fuel-cost pass-through effect common in regulated power) is Not verified; check on Screener before treating it as margin expansion. FY26 full year: net profit ₹5,117.6 crore, up 7.2% over FY25's ₹4,775.4 crore, after absorbing the ₹800 crore Mundra shutdown loss.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is down 26.2% from its September 2024 peak of ₹479.69 to ₹353.85. There is no recent demerger or split distorting this — the only corporate action on record is a 2011 stock split, already fully reflected in the price series — so this is a genuine price decline, not an artifact. Over 1 year the stock (-10.8%) has lagged both the Nifty (-9.5%) and peer NTPC (-5.2%). Over 3 years it has beaten the Nifty (40% vs 17%) and roughly matched NTPC (40% vs 39%). But over 5 years the gap to NTPC is stark: Tata Power is up 42% against NTPC's 149% — a large divergence that the stock's growth narrative has not closed, and recent price action suggests that gap is widening again rather than narrowing.
analysis.valuation_read: At a P/E of roughly 29.7x and P/B of about 2.8x, Tata Power trades well above what a plain regulated-generation utility typically commands. Why: the market is pricing in the renewables scale-up, EV charging, and new data-centre grid capex as a growth story rather than valuing it purely on current regulated earnings — the 0.71% dividend yield confirms cash is being reinvested, not returned. Whether that premium is justified is a separate question: ROE of 13.6% and ROCE of 11.6% are decent but not exceptional for the multiple being paid, and leverage (net debt/EBITDA of 3.34x) means a chunk of the growth is debt-funded, which raises the bar for execution.
analysis.growth_read: Growth looks genuinely volume-led in the parts that matter most: renewables capacity additions are scaling fast (419 MW added in Q2 FY27 alone, portfolio now 7.2 GW) and the core gen/T&D/renewables segment grew revenue 12% alongside EBITDA 12% and PAT 14% — margins and volumes are moving together, which is the healthier combination. The one figure to treat with caution is the solar manufacturing PAT's 'nearly 4x' jump, which is a small-base number from a business still ramping up, not representative of the group's overall margin trend.
analysis.health_read: Core operating cash generation looks fine — EBITDA is growing in the double digits and the regulated/renewables businesses are converting revenue into profit. The real concern is financial risk, not business risk: net debt stood at ₹56,122 crore (net debt/equity 1.18x, net debt/EBITDA 3.34x) even before the new ₹15,000 crore Mumbai data-centre grid commitment, and Q1 FY27 capex of ₹5,375 crore was the company's highest ever for a single quarter. Mundra also remains a specific asset-level risk: it already booked an ₹800 crore loss from a nine-month forced shutdown in FY26 and is currently operating only under a temporary government directive (through 31 Dec 2026) rather than a finalised commercial agreement with the procuring states.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter holding (Tata Sons 45.21% + Tata Steel 1.22% = 46.86% as of June 2026) has been stable and carries zero pledge — no leverage overhang from the promoter side. Institutional holding is split between FIIs (10.03%) and DIIs/mutual funds (around 18% combined). Not verified: whether any well-known individual investor holds a disclosable stake — nothing of that kind turned up in available sources, so none is named here rather than assumed absent.
strengths: Core generation, T&D and renewables PAT grew 14% YoY in Q1 FY27 on 12% revenue growth — profit growth is matched by volume growth, not just margin
Renewables execution is scaling quickly: 419 MW of utility-scale capacity added in Q2 FY27 alone (+130% YoY), taking the operating portfolio to 7.2 GW
Zero promoter pledge and a stable 46.86% promoter stake as of June 2026 — no leverage-driven governance overhang
Dividend has risen steadily from ₹1.30/share (2019) to ₹2.50/share (2026) even through a heavy capex cycle
watchpoints: Net debt of ₹56,122 crore (D/E 1.81x, net debt/EBITDA 3.34x) is rising further with a new ₹15,000 crore Mumbai grid commitment on top of record quarterly capex of ₹5,375 crore

Mundra's power-purchase agreement with procuring states is still not finalised; the plant runs today only under a government Section 11 directive valid through 31 December 2026, and a repeat of FY26's ₹800 crore shutdown loss is not ruled out if that directive lapses without a deal

Q4 FY26 revenue fell 12.85% YoY even as profit rose — the cause (likely a fuel pass-through effect) is Not verified; don't read this quarter as margin expansion without checking the underlying cost-recovery mechanics

The stock is down 26.2% from its September 2024 peak and has underperformed peer NTPC by roughly 100 percentage points over 5 years (42% vs 149%) — the premium 'growth' valuation has not been rewarded by the market lately
analysis.one_thing: Whether Tata Power finalises the Mundra SPPA with all five procuring states before the government's Section 11 directive expires on 31 December 2026 — that determines whether Mundra's cash flows become a durable contracted business or stay a recurring political/regulatory exposure. Q2 FY27 results on 11 November 2026 are the nearer-term checkpoint on debt and capex trajectory.
analysis.data_notes: Quarterly PAT/revenue/EBITDA figures for Q1 FY27, Q4 FY26 and FY26 were cross-checked across multiple financial-news outlets (Business Standard, Zeebiz, Angel One) and were consistent on PAT; one source quoted Q1 FY27 revenue as ₹18,898 crore versus the more commonly cited ₹19,051 crore — the latter cluster was used, and the discrepancy is noted rather than averaged. Valuation ratios (P/E, P/B, ROE, ROCE, D/E) and shareholding percentages were sourced from aggregator sites (ValueResearch, smart-investing.in) rather than the company's own filings — these should be cross-checked on Screener before being quoted precisely. The Mundra loss figure (₹800 crore) and the Section 11 extension timeline are corroborated across several reports but the exact SPPA finalisation timeline is Not verified — treat any specific date for resolution with caution.
